items.title: Recursa: Toward Recursively Self-Improving Foundation Model Systems
items.summary: Foundation models in changing environments can encounter unfamiliar domain knowledge that their original training did not cover. However, new domains rarely provide large amounts of expert-created training data or reliable supervisory signals for further training. We introduce Recursa, a foundation model system that adapts to new domains by learning from its own experience without human experts or a stronger teacher model. Recursa uses a knowledge repository to store what it learns: domain-specific skills and instructions on when to apply them, along with memories of past task experiences and …

items.title: SpecPilot: Autonomous Algorithm Discovery and Systems Optimization for Speculative Decoding
items.summary: Speculative decoding accelerates memory-bound LLM decoding with a lightweight drafter, and parallel drafters extend this speedup by drafting a whole block in one forward pass. However, it remains unclear whether their released systems (stock) attain the full speedup that parallel drafting permits. We identify three challenges. First, with one request, each step accepts few tokens but reads every target weight. Second, with batching, per-request verification work roughly halves the speedup over autoregressive (AR) decoding. items.title: ParetoSaddler: Pareto-Guided Optimization of Agent Harnesses for Quality and Cost
items.summary: Harness optimization can substantially improve LLM agents without modifying model weights, but existing methods primarily optimize response quality. Extending them to joint quality--cost optimization introduces a challenge: applying the deployment preference during intermediate updates can prematurely reject candidates that are valuable for later improvements. We introduce ParetoSaddler, which addresses this mismatch by separating intermediate candidate promotion from final deployment selection. items.title: MoviEdit: Long-form Multi-Shot Video Editing Made Easy
items.summary: Long-form multi-shot video editing requires an intended edit to remain coherent across abrupt changes in scene, viewpoint, and subject appearance, while processing substantially longer visual context than conventional single-shot editors. We introduce MoviEdit, an end-to-end framework for scalable long-form multi-shot video editing that jointly addresses the challenges of data, modeling, and evaluation. items.title: SeMo3D: Unifying 3D Generation, Editing, and Completion via Selective Modeling
items.summary: 3D generation, editing, and completion are typically treated as regenerating the complete 3D asset under task-specific constraints, even when only a local region needs modification. This leads to task isolation, inconsistency in content that should remain unchanged, and dependence on task-specific paired data. We address these issues with a key observation: the three tasks all synthesize a designated region while keeping the rest intact---the full region for generation, the target region for editing, and the missing region for completion. items.title: RoboColosseum: Evaluating Physical Intelligence at Scale In-The-Wild
items.summary: General-purpose robot policies must work across robots, tasks, and environments, yet the variation that makes physical trials informative also makes them difficult to reproduce. We introduce RoboColosseum, a distributed evaluation framework that combines unified policy serving and standardized protocols across a network of locally operated robots in diverse environments. Our initial study evaluates five vision-language-action (VLA) policies and three frontier AI agents across four embodiments (SO-101, Franka, Bimanual-YAM, and G1 Humanoid). items.title: StreamDuo: A Live Commentator and a Research Agent for Unseen Games
items.summary: Streaming video LLMs can now commentate live gameplay, but they are trained and tested on the same games. We study cross-game streaming commentary, in which a model trained on one game commentates games it has never seen, and find that current commentators transfer their timing but not their knowledge of the game world. We propose StreamDuo, which pairs a trainable commentator with a frozen research agent that reads the wiki of the game being played. items.title: A Tutorial on Generative Models for Music Audio
items.summary: Music audio generation spans instrumental clips, full songs with vocals, edits of existing recordings, and systems that play alongside a musician in real time. This monograph explains the methods behind these systems for readers familiar with neural-network training who are new to music generation. It introduces neural audio codecs and autoencoders, autoregressive and masked token models, diffusion and flow matching, sampling acceleration, and preference optimization in a shared notation. items.summary: Few-step autoregressive video diffusion enables efficient generation, yet maintaining consistency over long rollouts remains challenging, especially when subjects or scenes reappear after going out of sight. Despite progress in fidelity and rollout robustness, existing distillation methods do not fully exploit richer historical information to constrain the student's current prediction. To address this gap, we introduce History Forcing, a unified on-policy distillation framework that strengthens historical supervision for few-step autoregressive video generators. items.title: IdeaTaste: Do LLMs Share the Research Taste of Human Researchers?
items.summary: Research taste, the judgment of what to read, which problems to pursue, and which methods to try, increasingly shapes the work of AI scientists, yet it remains far less understood than their ability to execute research. We introduce IdeaTaste, a benchmark that scores an LLM by how closely the research proposals it writes from a literature snapshot frozen at 2025 match the work the same communities published in 2026. items.title: Order-Only On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own generations by matching the teacher's token probabilities. These probabilities entangle two kinds of information: which tokens the teacher prefers, and how confident it is. The latter reflects the teacher's own capacity and calibration, which a smaller student may be unable to reproduce. Because the teacher temperature changes these values without changing the ordering, OPD is also sensitive to the temperature choice. items.title: Advancing SVD-based LLM Compression via Layer-Wise Error Model Search
items.summary: Low-rank SVD-based compression offers a powerful strategy to reduce the computational costs of LLMs. However, existing methods face two key limitations: (i) global rank allocation, where uncalibrated error proxies fail to capture complex error propagation, and (ii) decomposition quality, where Fisher-based estimators suffer from severe rank collapse. items.title: DAMI: Dual-Axis Memory Initialization for Enhanced Long-Context Retrieval in Gated Linear Attention
items.summary: Linear attention scales linearly with sequence length, but its finite-state memory can limit long-context retrieval. In gated linear recurrences, memory retention depends on state decay, which is shaped jointly by gate parameters A_log and dt_bias and by input activations. In controlled Gated DeltaNet (GDN) experiments, both parameters remain highly correlated with their initial values after training, highlighting the importance of initialization. items.title: DR Pixel: Page-Native Deep Research with Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Complex documents such as scientific papers contain rich information in tables, figures, and equations; however, existing deep research (DR) agents typically reduce papers to OCR-extracted text. We instead ask whether vision-language models (VLMs) can enable page-native deep research: directly retrieving and reasoning over rendered document page images. We introduce DR Pixel, the first open-source end-to-end multimodal DR agent that uses rendered page images as its sole retrieval and reasoning unit, operating over a corpus of 1.06M pages. items.title: Cross-Primitive Consistency in Jev
items.summary: Jev enables efficient decision-making with large language models (LLMs) through typed querying primitives, allowing the same semantic state to be expressed in different formats, such as binary and multiple-choice queries. However, the consistency of decisions across primitives has not been systematically evaluated. This work introduces PrimaCons, a four-axis benchmark for assessing cross-primitive consistency while preserving the semantics of the query. items.title: Multi-Agent Relay Thinking
items.summary: Existing multi-agent collaboration (MAC) methods have primarily explored a group thinking collaboration topology, where agents independently generate solutions and aggregate their outputs. In this work, we investigate an alternative relay thinking topology, where reasoning ownership is dynamically transferred across agents, allowing subsequent agents to inherit and refine an evolving reasoning trajectory. items.title: Where Do Vision Language Models Fail at 3D Reasoning?
items.summary: Vision-language models can get individual judgments right while struggling to recover and consistently use the exact properties of a 3D object. To characterize this gap, we introduce BedBench, a controlled benchmark of thirteen procedurally generated tasks spanning individual judgments and composite answers. Across twelve open-weight and four frontier models, per-color counting exposes a pronounced weakness: humans achieve 93.3% accuracy, compared with 7.2% for the best model. items.summary: Coding agents solve repository issues through long sequences of exploration, editing, and validation. These trajectories are increasingly used as post-training data, so how they are collected shapes what the trained model learns. A common approach is to sample multiple trajectories independently for each issue and then select or curate them. items.title: LEANGUARD: Lean-Verified Guardrails for Tool-Using Agents
items.summary: Tool-using language-model agents often execute actions that their domain policies forbid. We present LeanGuard, a runtime that checks every proposed tool call against a policy written in Lean4 before the call reaches the environment. Policies combine state predicates with scoped past-time temporal operators over the execution history, evaluation is fail-closed, and the decision procedure is proved equivalent to a LeanLTL semantics. items.title: Advances in Agentic Computer Graphics
items.summary: Computer graphics is built on code. Large language model (LLM) agents can now generate graphics code and iteratively refine it through various feedback. This capability opens the door to a potentially new paradigm of computer graphics, with graphics algorithms increasingly built around agentic systems to automate progressively complex tasks. Over the past years, research on agentic graphics has expanded rapidly across a diverse range of tasks. items.summary: Prediction errors from video world models are often treated as physical surprise, but they can also reflect appearance, static content, motion, or ordinary prediction difficulty. We present an evaluation framework that separates what frozen representations contain, how they organize appearance and physical differences, and what changes a model's own prediction error. items.title: TaoMate-FVSR:Audio-Guided Facial Video Restoration
items.summary: AI-generated videos often depict people within detailed scenes while leaving their small facial regions poorly resolved. Visual super-resolution can sharpen these regions without resolving whether the recovered lips and teeth agree with the spoken audio. We present an audio-guided facial video restoration framework that addresses this ambiguity within a reference-guided video flow model. items.title: PhotoGuider: Composition-Aware Cropping and 360^{circ} View Framing with Explainable Photographic Assessments
items.summary: Traditional image cropping assumes the photograph already contains the composition worth keeping, and asks only where to crop. A full 360^{circ} scene offers no such guarantee: the viewing direction in a scene has to be discovered before anything can be framed. We present PhotoGuider, a measure-then-frame method that answers both questions with compact learned scorers over one shared set of composition-aware features. items.title: Training Specialist LLMs on Your Phone: Forward-Only Optimization via Block-Spectral Coordinates
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) on personal devices keep user data local, but limited memory restricts their general capability. Since most user-specific tasks do not require the breadth of frontier models, a practical solution is to adapt a shared on-device model into lightweight specialists. However, backpropagation is prohibitive in memory, and users rarely provide labeled data. items.title: Accelerating Offloading-Based MoE Inference by Interleaving Concurrent Requests
items.summary: Expert offloading enables large mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models to run locally, but conventional batching stalls the GPU while missing experts are fetched. items.summary: Reinforcement learning objectives that maximize expected return can concentrate probability mass on a small subset of high-reward outcomes, limiting diversity when multiple distinct solutions are desirable. We introduce Density-Aware Reward Scaling (DARS), a simple reward-processing mechanism that promotes reward-proportional sampling in continuous outcome spaces while retaining standard policy-gradient training. items.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become an effective approach for improving mathematical reasoning in large language models. However, a fundamental question remains: when a model fails to solve a problem, does it truly lack the underlying capability? items.summary: Large language models are candidates for collecting and analyzing records in criminal investigations and mass surveillance. Real deployments lack the ground truth needed to score a model's conclusions, and no benchmark evaluates these capabilities in a simulated environment. items.summary: SAE-based feature-level interventions to suppress PII leakage in LLMs are primarily evaluated by log-probability reduction. items.summary: In single-pixel (ghost) imaging, known illumination patterns probe an object and a detector with no spatial resolution returns one number per pattern. Each measurement costs acquisition time and photons and, for ionizing probes, contributes to delivered dose. items.summary: Split Inference (SI) addresses the hardware resource limitations of Internet of Things (IoT) devices by distributing tiny Machine Learning (TinyML) model segments across multiple IoT devices. items.summary: We study cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning with decoupled dynamics and a monotone submodular reward function over joint trajectories. items.summary: A deployed LLM coaching agent answers requests whose correct response depends on player state and game version, so advice that is right for one player can be wrong for the next. items.title: 腾讯12.8亿用户蝉联中国互联网第一，绿泡泡月活破1.5亿，手游top10独占8款
items.summary: 11 月 3 日，QuestMobile发布最新《中国移动互联网秋季大报告》。报告显示，截至 2026 年 9 月，腾讯控股以 12.80 亿去重总用户量（APP + 小程序）位列中国互联网公司用户规模榜首，第九年蝉联榜首，霸主地位稳固。 短剧业务是本次报告的关注重点。腾讯旗下嵌入微信生态的绿泡泡短剧2026年9月月活跃用户规模达到 1.56 亿，登顶微信小程序短剧月活榜。该产品依托微信社交关系链与视频号导流快速起量，目前体量已是短剧行业第二名，增长速度很快。 游戏业务方面，2026 年 9 月手机游戏 App 月活跃用户 TOP10 中，腾讯独占 8 款，合计月活约 3.41 亿。其中，王者荣耀以 1.29 亿月活位居全行业第二，仅次于乐元素开心消消乐的 1.61 亿；三角洲行动、和平精英分别以 6675 万、3547 万月活位列第三、第四。报告同时提到，名古屋亚运会期间，王者荣耀以庞大玩家基数成为电竞项目顶流。 报告指出，短剧视频与短视频已成为驱动全网用户时长增长的核心引擎，增长贡献率达 111.5%。依托微信社交与私域流量，小程序短剧起量迅猛，短剧业务正成为腾讯盘活流量矩阵的重要抓手。

items.title: 香港大学发布全球首个KYA报告关注智能体信任建设，九类企业实践获收录
items.summary: 11月3日，香港大学副校长汪扬教授与香港大学经管学院杨宏副教授代表香港大学KYA课题组，在2026年香港金融科技周 x StartmeupHK创业节发布全球首个KYA（Know Your Agent）领域报告《KYA：智能体信用体系研究报告》。 报告聚焦智能体参与真实经济活动后的身份、授权、信用与责任问题，结合109份从业者有效问卷及包含Stripe、蚂蚁数科等近十个企业案例，提出智能体成熟度模型、KYA框架和智能体发展指数，并进一步探讨“智能体信任资本”的形成及其经济价值。 “没有KYA，就没有智能体经济。”报告认为，模型能力的提升不会自动转化为商业上的可委托性。只有当身份可确权、履约可核验、权限可约束时，智能体才能获得与其能力相匹配的经济授权。KYA所要解决的，正是智能体从技术可能走向商业可行的问题。 香港大学副校长汪扬教授与香港大学经管学院杨宏副教授发布全球首个KYA领域报告 智能体加速进入真实经济，信任赤字正侵蚀人工智能红利 报告将智能体的演进概括为四个阶段：能力智能体、执行智能体、交易智能体和经济智能体。截至目前，行业整体仍处于从能力智能体向执行智能体加速演进的阶段，部分前沿场景已开始探索交易智能体。 从执行任务走向跨主体交易，意味着智能体需要获得企业内部流程之外的信任。采购、支付或专业服务智能体可以在授权范围内代表用户采取行动，但交易对手仍需确认其代表谁、获得何种授权、…

items.title: 小孩子看稍微暴力血腥一点的电影真的影响很大么
items.summary: 不到该看的年龄，却看了，昆汀接受采访的时候，说他就是这样长大的，他的妈妈不会太限制他观影，所以同龄的孩子不能看的电影他在很小的时候就看过，从小看电影的量就很大。后来不也成为出名的导演有所成就了么。相同类型的还有电影某种物质的导演科拉莉法尔雅。 还有印象就是亚当桑德勒的人生遥控器里，讲他的小孩子已经在看断手断脚找分尸的剧情了，所以有此一问，小孩子看稍微暴力血腥一点的电影真的影响很大么 重点来了，我有一个朋友。他家里小孩 6 岁，他爱看动作电影、好莱坞大片，经常出现一些打斗、暴力的场面，娃有的时候会跟着一起看。当小孩面看的当然不是 B 级片、cult 片，就是普通的战争打斗、功夫格斗。如果现在不适合让他一起看，那几岁适合。 要知道，我们可是从小看《聊斋》《黑太阳 731 》《 XX 功纪录片》长大的啊。。。
